method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading, formula and diagram-code comparison, reverse paraphrase and bounded fact checking; not independent or human review.
scope: All ten translated content blocks in the real-line section, including the theorem, two proofs, TikZ diagram, historical aside and least-upper-bound discussion.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Reals are to be constructed from rationals. Both form ordered fields, but there are strictly more reals, and irrational reals such as square root of two have long been known.
samples.checks: The ordered-field reference, cardinal comparison, Cantor attribution, irrational definition and labeled theorem all remain present.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Assuming square root of two is a reduced natural-number fraction gives m²=2n². The formal proof makes m and then n even, contradicting reducibility.
samples.checks: Every equality, parity implication and commented align formula is preserved; the conclusion remains a contradiction with lowest terms.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The geometric proof compares the overlap and uncovered areas of two n-side squares, yielding a smaller p/q representation of square root of two and an infinite-descent contradiction.
samples.checks: TikZ commands, dimensions, labels, citation, area equation, inequalities and membership statement have exact structural parity.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Completeness distinguishes the reals: every nonempty upper-bounded set of reals has a least upper bound. The rationals below square root of two have upper bounds but no rational least upper bound, while the continuum is intended to fill all rational-line gaps.
samples.checks: The property quantifiers, set-builder disjunction, explicit bound 3, failure of a rational least upper bound and continuum conclusion are all retained.

source_observations.finding: A disabled source footnote incorrectly assigns both roots to the radical symbol.
source_observations.resolution: Corrected only in the inactive Marathi footnote with adjacent note; active reader content is unaffected.

source_observations.finding: The source gives Tennenbaum's death year as 2006; his memorial records 4 May 2005.
source_observations.resolution: Marathi uses 1927–2005 with an adjacent note; the uncertain birth-year range is explicitly documented in the issue ledger.

limitations: No independent linguistic or mathematical certification has been performed.
